ideas.description: Revert the tip's bs-1024 late phases. Base: E116 code (82e6219). Precondition, free (H4.2.4): log the source hash and a one-line diff against 82e6219. Change only the batch size of the 28 px and 32 px phases, from 1024 to 1536. Keep the sample-indexed schedule (LR warmup/decay, floor-hold, renorm cadence and the 85% freeze point all in samples). Rescale the SGD groups (BN biases, whitening bias, head bias) in those phases by the kilostep rule. Keep the Muon lr x1.25 at 32 px and momentum 0.6. Keep the final-EMA window and lookahead stop pinned to the last 8 steps. Compile static bs-1536 28/32 px graphs and warm every freeze x renorm x whiten-bias-grad variant for the new shapes in build. Verify on a 2-trial dev run with TORCH_LOGS=recompiles that nothing compiles after build. Accuracy is decided untimed through the benchmark trial code on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process, against the pooled ~198-trajectory E116 baseline (SE ~0.032). Add one scored run with per-trial prepare/train logs to measure the real time.
ideas.expected: Time -2.0 to -2.5% vs the 4.26 s tip (about 4.15-4.18 s), from ~90 fewer 32/28 px steps at ~1.7 ms each. E121 (99 seeds) found extra updates worth +0.004 pp, so my central accuracy estimate is -0.03 ± 0.04 pp (population mean ~0.7515-0.7522). Bankable only if the paired loss is <= 0.03 pp and the arm mean is >= 0.7518. A further 100 seeds then confirm before banking under H4.9. If the loss is 0.03-0.08 pp, it becomes a funded candidate, to be paired with whichever accuracy source lands. If the loss is >= 0.1 pp, the bs-1024 tail was a real purchase despite E121, and H2.11 closes.

ideas.description: Depth cut arm (a), 2/3/3. Base: E116 code. Remove group-1 conv3 (with its BN and GELU) so group 1 is conv1 plus a single-conv residual branch. Re-batch the Muon filter stacks for the changed counts, including the frozen-group-1 update variant. Rebuild the dirac init over the remaining convs. Warm every (resolution, batch) x freeze x renorm x whiten-bias-grad variant in build, and check on a 2-trial dev run with TORCH_LOGS=recompiles that nothing compiles after build. Change nothing else: schedule, 85% freeze, tail. Before deciding, run an untimed per-step profile of the modified net at all four shapes (with the frozen 32 px variant) and project total time over the E116 schedule, because E123's -7.6% was measured with the freeze off. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled ~198-trajectory E116 baseline. Score once only if the loss is <= 0.35 pp.
ideas.expected: Projected time -6.5 to -7.5% (about 3.95-4.0 s); slightly less than E123's 7.6% because the freeze already removes group-1 backward over the last 15%. My central accuracy estimate is -0.15 to -0.35 pp (capacity on the 31x31 maps; SGD-era capacity cuts cost ~0.1 pp per 1%). If the loss is <= ~0.25 pp (<= 0.035 pp per 1%, judged against the slope that the H2.10.6 arms measure), queue a funded variant that re-spends ~half the saving on 32 px epochs to restore mu >= 0.7521, for a net ~-3 to -4%. If the loss is >= 0.4 pp, this cut is worse than the slope.

ideas.description: Measure the local yardstick on the tip. Base: E116 code. Two untimed arms through the benchmark trial code, each on seeds 3-102 in its own fresh process: (A) 32 px phase -0.25 epoch (2.5 instead of 2.75), (B) 32 px phase +0.25 epoch (3.0). Index everything by samples (LR warmup/decay, floor-hold, renorm cadence, Muon x1.25 phase factor). Keep the freeze at 85% of the new total samples and the final-EMA/lookahead window pinned to the last 8 steps. All shapes are already static and warmed. Compare each arm with the pooled ~198-trajectory E116 baseline. For the scored row, rerun the E116 tip unchanged, which adds another distinct gate sample (H4.9.1).
ideas.expected: Time per arm about ±0.11 s (±2.5%). Accuracy: A about -0.08 to -0.20 pp, B about +0.05 to +0.15 pp, i.e. a slope of 0.03-0.07 pp per 1%, resolved to ±0.035 pp per arm. This rate is the bar for the depth cuts, group-3 width 512, the bs-1536 revert and 12 px swaps, and it sizes how many re-spent 32 px samples a depth cut must buy back. If B gains >= 0.1 pp, re-spending into 32 px is an efficient funding source. If B gains <= 0.03, the slope is concave above the tip and funded cuts must come from elsewhere.

ideas.description: FreezeOut-style anneal before the 85% freeze, arm (a) only. Base: E116 code. Over 75%-85% of samples, ramp the LR multiplier of the group-1 filters (Muon) and the stem/group-1 BN params (SGD) linearly from 1 to 0, then detach at 85% exactly as now. Use separate 0-d LR tensors for the group-1 Muon stack and the group-1 SGD group, written host-side so nothing recompiles; if the group-1 filters currently share a stacked Muon update with others, scale their slice by a 0-d per-stack factor. All other groups, the schedule and the tail are unchanged. Time is unchanged. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled ~198-trajectory E116 baseline.
ideas.expected: Time equal to the tip (±0.3%). Accuracy +0.02 to +0.06 pp over E116, recovering part of the ~0.09 pp freeze cost by removing the hard switch at a nonzero LR. A gain of >= +0.064 pp (2 SE) makes it a zero-time margin source that restores mu to ~E100's level. That would fund the bs-1536 revert or let the freeze move to ~80%. A result within ±0.03 pp means the freeze cost is lost late adaptation, not the discontinuity, and arm (b) (BN eval in the frozen window) becomes the only remaining refinement.

ideas.description: Depth cut arm (b), 3/3/2. Base: E116 code. Remove group-3 conv3 (with its BN and GELU) so group 3 is conv1 plus a single-conv residual branch. Re-batch the Muon stacks, rebuild the dirac init, warm every shape x freeze x renorm variant in build, and check with a TORCH_LOGS=recompiles dev run. Change nothing else. Run an untimed per-step profile with the freeze on and project total time over the E116 schedule. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled E116 baseline. Run this after arm (a), so that if both arms qualify they can be compared at equal projected saving.
ideas.expected: Projected time -5.5 to -6.5% (about 4.0-4.03 s); the group-3 backward is untouched by the group-1 freeze, so most of E123's -6.1% should survive. Accuracy is a low prior: -0.2 to -0.45 pp, because late capacity was valuable on CIFAR-100 (E005, and futurebiohackers chose 576 for this). If its loss per 1% is lower than arm (a)'s and <= the H2.10.6 slope, it becomes the depth-cut candidate for a funded re-spend. If both arms lose >= 1.5x their slope equivalent, depth cuts close.

ideas.description: Lookahead removal re-measured on the large-seed instrument, which gates H9.2.1. Base: E116 code. Remove the lookahead-EMA entirely: the net trains on its own weights; its buffers and foreach kernels are dropped from build and the step loop. Keep the floor-hold, the final 8-step EMA (lerp 0.3 every 4 steps), eval on the EMA weights with BN buffers from the net, and the 85% freeze. Change nothing else. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled ~198-trajectory E116 baseline. Add one scored run with per-trial logs, because the expected time saving is inside single-run noise.
ideas.expected: Time -0.3 to -0.5% (about 4.24-4.25 s; E092 saved 0.4%). H9.2 predicts a loss of >= 0.1 pp; my central estimate is -0.05 to -0.15 pp, since E092's -0.18 was 8 seeds (~1.4 SE) and regresses toward zero. If the loss is >= 0.1 pp, lookahead is real smoothing, and the H9.2.1 strength arms (ramp exponent, peak decay, final-EMA lerp) get queued as zero-time accuracy sources. If the loss is <= 0.04 pp, H9.2 closes; the ~0.4% is banked only together with an accuracy source, because the margin is gone.

structured_output.summary:
I added six ideas, all built on the current tip (E116 code: 85% freeze, about 4.26 s, population mean 0.7521) and all judged on 100 seeds against the pooled ~198-trajectory E116 baseline. The queue now has 7 queued ideas plus I133, which is running. I dropped nothing: I134 (translate 4, on the E100 base) is still a valid paired test.

**Highest priority:**
- **Batch size back to 1536 in the 28/32 px phases (H2.11.6, priority 5).** Expected -2 to -2.5% time. E121 (99 seeds) suggests the bs-1024 tail buys nothing, so the expected accuracy loss is about 0 to -0.05 pp. It is bankable only if the 100-seed mean stays at or above 0.7518.

**Priority 4:**
- **Measure the local yardstick (H2.10.6).** Two arms, 32 px phase -0.25 and +0.25 epoch. The measured slope sets the bar every later cut must beat, and tells us how many 32 px epochs a depth cut must buy back.
- **Depth cut 2/3/3 (H2.18.2a).** Projected -6.5 to -7.5% time with the freeze on. Expected loss -0.15 to -0.35 pp. If the loss trades better than the slope, a follow-up spends part of the saving on extra 32 px epochs.

**Priority 3 and below:**
- **Anneal group-1 LR to 0 before the freeze (H2.20.5a).** Zero time cost. It may recover +0.02 to +0.06 pp of the freeze's cost.
- **Depth cut 3/3/2 (H2.18.2b).** Explore arm. Projected about -6% time, but the prior for accuracy is low because late capacity has been valuable on CIFAR-100.
- **Lookahead removal on 100 seeds (H9.2.2).** This gates the averaging-strength arms (H9.2.1). Expected time saving is only about 0.4%.

Because the margin is gone (0.7521 against the 0.7518 floor), every cut that costs accuracy is framed as needing an accuracy source to pay for it. Each idea also requires checking the source hash against its stated base (H4.2.4).
